title: Customize hits template

comments.body: @redox The goal is for the user to iterate on the hits in a hogan template rather than being only able to provide an item template.
Both ways are acceptable, and have tradeoffs. What is your use case @proudlygeek ? :D

@bobylito @redox currently is impossible to use external plugins which relies on _data-_ attributes for configuration. An example is [Masonry](http://masonry.desandro.com/) (see also issue #736).

Right now the only _clean_ way to achieve this is to write a custom widgets which basically wraps the hits one. I think it could make sense to add an esclusive `items` template property to override the inner react map.

I think the idea fits the `hits` widget scope. This is an advanced option because users will then have to handle everything themselves, but I see how this can be useful.

Regarding Masonry, I'm not sure a jQuery plugin that reorders DOM elements (if that's what it's doing) will play well with React, though.

@pixelastic I think the point here is to make Masonry or similar reorder our React components on the DOM. It shouldn't make any assumptions on the underlying technology stack. It should treat them as black boxes.

@proudlygeek yep, I agree, but React can get really picky with what other libraries are doing with its DOM. But still, I agree that we should to make it work with Masonry. We can tackle that together after the holydays if you'd like.
As seen with #748 we may want to use tables, which is impossible right now and would be doable with the `hits` template property.
